reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch treat David's armor-bearer role as an honorary title, not continuous service, so Saul's 17:55 question seeks the father's standing, not David's identity.

discrepancy.note: Paine flags 1 Samuel 16 and 17 as two accounts that contradict each other on how Saul and David first became acquainted.

quotes.text: I observed two chapters in I Samuel (xvi. and xvii.) that contradict each other with respect to David, and the manner he became acquainted with Saul; as Jeremiah xxxvii. and xxxviii. contradict each other with respect to the cause of Jeremiah's imprisonment.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), note, on 1 Samuel 16 and 17.

sides.snippet: David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armor bearer.
sides.verseText: David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armor bearer.

sides.snippet: Abner, whose son is this youth? Abner said, As your soul lives, O king, I can't tell.
sides.verseText: When Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son is this youth? Abner said, As your soul lives, O king, I can't tell.
